idiom_name: std::variant state + visitor reducer + subscriber list (Qt signals/slots when Qt is already in the stack)
implementation_notes: C++ has no stream type and no built-in observable, so the roles are hand-assembled: states as std::variant<...> (a type-safe union whose alternatives are visited with std::visit), events as a second variant or as lightweight structs, and a component exposing state(), dispatch(Event) and subscribe(std::function<void(const State&)>) with a subscriber list guarded by a mutex or confined to one thread. Qt, when it is already in the stack, supplies the observer half directly - signals are emitted when a QObject's state changes and are delivered to any number of slots, with connections cleaned up automatically when either end is destroyed - so the component becomes a QObject with a stateChanged(State) signal that widgets or QML bindings consume; RxCpp is the alternative when a full reactive pipeline is wanted.
pitfalls: Subscribers are std::function objects capturing raw pointers or references; nothing unregisters them on destruction, so return a scoped connection token or tie subscribers to the component's lifetime.
Re-entrancy: calling dispatch from inside a subscriber while the list is being iterated invalidates the iteration - queue the state change and drain it outside the loop.
std::variant becomes valueless_by_exception when an alternative's assignment throws; keep alternatives nothrow-movable and check the index when recovering.
A second thread reading state without synchronization sees a torn value: publish under a mutex, an atomic shared_ptr, or confine the component to the UI or io_context thread.
